items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had four uncles. All of them played drums... Louis . . . and Lucien [Barbarin] was great. He was a great drummer too.

ctx.x: The Barbarin family is one of the most popular names in New Orleans music with names like Paul and Louis and Isidore. How is your mother related to them?

That’s her brothers you call. Paul’s a brother. Willie’s a brother. Lucien’s a brother. Paul, Willie, Lucien, and Louis. They all played music, because my whole family . . . We were encouraged to play music, because it added to the poor folk’s moneybag. It added a little money more to the . . . You played as a extra to your regular job, whatever you . . . was your profession or your trade. Mostly your trade. By playing music, you added on weekends or anytime, you added to the moneybags in the family.
So it was an honor to be a musician.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: I've got four uncles -- Paul Barbarin, Louis Barbarin, Lucien Barbarin, Willie Barbarin.

ctx.x: I just want to get back a little so we won't digress too far, Danny. When you were a kid around New Orleans, when did you first start to think about getting into music?

Well, I didn't think about it too much. I was going to school. And I'm hearing this music all the time, and I'd see these musicians, they're celebrated. I've got four uncles -- Paul Barbarin, Louis Barbarin, Lucien Barbarin, Willie Barbarin. We live in the neighborhood, in the Seventh Ward, where there's quite a few halls -- the (?) Hall, the Jean Ami Hall, the Franz(?) Ami Hall, the New Hall. And on Ledgerfield Avenue there was about four or five White halls. And there was music all the time. And I'm listening…

And my uncles... My grandfather being in the brass band, he played the funerals with the Onward Brass Band, which was the greatest brass band at that time. And there was a rivalry between Manny Perez and George Moret(?), who was the leader of the Excelsior Band. And I'm hearing this. And my uncles, they're talkin' about who's who and who ain't. And it's a celebrate thing, and everybody is celebrated. So they would talk who could play and who couldn't, and who rated... Like most people, the kids in town, they…
